class.name: PerformanceColumnSummary
class.brief_description: Statistics of one column of a [PerformanceRecorder] run.
class.description: A [PerformanceColumnSummary] holds the number of samples, the minimum, maximum and mean, and the 50th, 95th and 99th percentiles of one recorded column over the whole run. Get it from [method PerformanceSummary.get_column]. Values are in the unit of the column: microseconds for the time builtins, bytes for memory. Minimum, maximum and mean are always exact. The percentiles are exact while the whole run fits in the ring buffer of the recorder ([method is_exact]); for longer runs they are estimated from a log-scaled histogram with 8 buckets per power of two and are at most 9.05% away from the exact value (typically 2-4%). [codeblocks] [gdscript] var frame_time = PerformanceRecorder.get_summary().get_column("frame_time") print("p95: %.1f ms, max: %.1f ms" % [frame_time.get_p95() / 1000.0, frame_time.get_maximum() / 1000.0]) [/gdscript] [csharp] var frameTime = PerformanceRecorder.GetSummary().GetColumn("frame_time"); GD.Print($"p95: {frameTime.GetP95() / 1000.0:F1} ms, max: {frameTime.GetMaximum() / 1000.0:F1} ms"); [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: get_histogram
method.description: Returns how many samples fall into each range between [param limits], which must be in ascending order. The result has one more element than [param limits]: element [code]i[/code] counts the samples that are less than or equal to [code]limits[i][/code] and greater than [code]limits[i - 1][/code]; the last element counts the samples above the last limit. For example, a frame-time histogram with [code][8333, 16667, 33333][/code] returns the frames that ran at 120 FPS or faster, at 60 FPS, at 30 FPS, and slower. For runs longer than the ring buffer the counts are estimated from the histogram buckets.

method.name: get_maximum
method.description: Returns the largest value of the column. [code]0.0[/code] if there are no samples.

method.name: get_mean
method.description: Returns the average value of the column. [code]0.0[/code] if there are no samples.

method.name: get_minimum
method.description: Returns the smallest value of the column. [code]0.0[/code] if there are no samples.

method.name: get_name
method.description: Returns the name of the column, as in the CSV header and [method PerformanceRecorder.get_column_names].

method.name: get_p50
method.description: Returns the median (50th percentile) of the column.

method.name: get_p95
method.description: Returns the 95th percentile of the column: 95% of the samples are less than or equal to this value.

method.name: get_p99
method.description: Returns the 99th percentile of the column: 99% of the samples are less than or equal to this value.

method.name: get_percentile
method.description: Returns any percentile of the column, [param percentile] between [code]0.0[/code] (the minimum) and [code]100.0[/code] (the maximum). Values between two samples are interpolated linearly. Returns [code]0.0[/code] if there are no samples.

method.name: get_sample_count
method.description: Returns the number of values in the column. Empty cells (for example a gauge that was never set) are not counted.

method.name: is_exact
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the percentiles were computed from all samples, [code]false[/code] if they were estimated from the histogram because the run was longer than the ring buffer.
